reviews.full_transcript: Hey everyone. Heat. Heat. N. [music] Heat. [music] Heat. [music] >> [music] [music] >> The F1 Bandit is probably one of the most well-known kite models in the industry since the beginning of kite surfing. Through the collaboration with Brainchild, this model has now been re-imagined. The front tube is now suspended with a seven-point bridal without pulley. The steering lines go to a small V and are not adjustable. Inflation and deflation are handled on one hand by a large single type inlet and outlet valve, but also separately by an additional valve, which allows you to release the air even faster. The one pump system is short and kept absolutely straight. The front tube is made from a high strength dacron material and is welded using pro belt technology. This means the layers are welded together and the cut edges are covered with a fine webbing. This is not stitching that serves for stability. It is only there so that no open cut edges are visible or can be felt. Line deflectors are only present at the ends of the front tube. The cross struts, three in total, do not have any line deflectors. Regarding the struts, it should be mentioned again that they are also made of a high strength dacron material which however is coated on the inside resulting in greater stiffness of these struts. According to the manufacturer, a completely new material is also used here for the canopy fabric. Based on the structure, it's hard to tell whether it's a double riptop or a triple riptop because it doesn't appear completely uniform. I would say it's a double riptop. In the area of the trailing edge, a fine mesh triple riptop material is used. The trailing edge is simply hemmed again. And on both sides, we have two plastic batterns each so that the trailing edge can't flutter excessively. The cross struts are each attached to the canopy with a single seam and are doubled and glued from the inside. On the banded brainchild, impact or abrasion points are only reinforced with fabric strips. And at the transition from the front tube to the canopy, there is of course another fabric strip as reinforcement. The combination of an airflow that attaches very early to the slightly more elongated profile than what we've seen before, a medium baseline pull, and a noticeably higher flight speed ensures that you get up on the board very early in all disciplines. That is you start planning or get on the foil. Even in the lowest wind range compared to the previous bandids, it needs to be moved less to produce maximum performance. The new Bandit brainchild also delivers strong performance when sailing upwind. It holds a very stable position far out at the edge of the wind window and no corrections are needed in terms of positioning. The canopy remains absolutely stable. And as mentioned, there is nothing you need to correct here. The kite doesn't fall back, but instead pulls cleanly and willingly to windward. The bar feeling here can simply be described as excellent in terms of response to steering commands and directness, but also comfort at the same time. This is really a very nice experience. The steering works very harmoniously here thanks to the absolutely precise support of the front tube. It turns very smoothly in all situations, but at the same time, there's always a slight sense that it's well damped and comfortable. That's simply due to the choice of canopy fabric. And that perfectly completes the homogeneous flight behavior and the feeling along with the consistently moderate bar pressure. As already mentioned at the beginning, when gliding, the Bandit Brainchild has a consistently moderate base pull. You can really play with the power delivery of the bandit brainchild depending on what maneuver you want to do or when you're riding a wave with a surfboard. And depending on where you move it in the wind window and how you steer it, you can create either a gentle power profile, so not too high of a power peak, or it can also be explosive. If you steer it quickly and sharply, it can increase its flight speed and accordingly generate an impressive power peak. Let's move on to its overall flight characteristics. Its turning ability is very tight and always smooth. In doing so, it develops a high flight speed. You can depower this kite very variably, meaning you can bring it deeper into the wind window during kite loops or in a more guided style in the waves. It really follows very well. It has excellent positioning and because it also feels dampened through the canopy, the overall sensation is very homogeneous and controlled. In terms of flight stability, it delivers good to very good performance because the canopy isn't as stiff as an Alula frame. Instead, the optimal feel and performance are achieved by adjusting the profile through the canopy fabric, the construction of the leading edge, and also the choice of fabric. This combination works truly uniquely well here. >> [music] >> When we've tested the latest Bandit model in recent years, we've honestly never really rated it higher than simply good in the waves because due to the necessary compromise for riding performance, there was always just a bit too much of a noticeable power peak that you couldn't really get rid of no matter what you tried. With the new model, this interplay is such that on the one hand, you have a very fast, very tight turning kite that remains completely responsive on the bar even when depowered. That's already an absolutely positive point, but other models have had that before as well. But here, since the canopy or the overall construction now dampens part of the power spike, if you position the kite correctly and don't make the steering movements too abrupt, so you don't accelerate it too much, then the whole thing becomes a really great experience for strapless surfing in the waves. Additionally, you don't really need to move it much since it also delivers excellent performance while drifting. In this regard, it can definitely hold its own against good wave kites. [music] Since the kite responds quickly to steering commands even in very light wind, and the overall flight characteristics are consistent and easy to understand, this kite also has the potential to make kite foilers happy. [music] Let me address the question, why does the branded brainchild actually jump better than its predecessors? I have simply established this thesis for now. This is because we have a slightly higher aspect ratio and a higher flight speed. Additionally, the kite is able to generate vertical lift more easily when loading up than the previous models. Of course, the hang time also increases due to the higher aspect ratio. And if you were familiar with the previous Bandits and now fly this model, you'll truly be amazed at how much higher the performance is with this one. In fact, its performance can already be compared to that of some free ride higherformance kites. The basic concept that the Bandit from F1 is meant to be everybody's darling hasn't really changed here. Now, within this one-sall concept, it impresses with a new sporty touch that surpasses the performance of those we've tested so far. And the whole thing is just even easier to access. So you really don't have to have improved your own writing skills if you switch from one of the other models. You'll notice that things just work out overall more easily than before. And the necessary riding skills for this kite are basically suitable even for beginners since the entire concept is implemented so seamlessly and in crucial moments there is a damping effect available which means that control and easy handling are immediately accessible to anyone regardless of gender. For our test the bandit brainchide was available in 9 square meters along with the new bar. There will also be a separate video about this in the next few days. And we can say very clearly, no matter what conditions we had, no matter what we had under our feet, whether it was a foil, a twin tip, or a surfboard, the fun was always absolutely optimal. In the end, of course, the question arises, how much does the whole thing cost? Nine square meters come in at a recommended retail price of €2,100. And it's clear to say that for this particular price, a truly remarkable and genuinely impressive new feeling has been created here with a very well-known and familiar concept.
reviews.summary: Gleiten tv conducted a thorough technical and on-water review of the 2025 Bandit Brainchild, praising its new seven-point bridle, high-strength dacron construction, and novel canopy fabric for creating a uniquely dampened yet responsive feel. They were particularly impressed by the kite's improved wave performance — a known weakness of previous Bandits — and noted the higher aspect ratio delivers a clear jump performance upgrade. Tested across foil, twin-tip, and surfboard in a 9m, they rated it as genuinely impressive at its €2,100 price point.

structured_review.summary: The 2025 F-One Bandit Brainchild is a meaningful evolution of the iconic all-around kite, now featuring a higher aspect ratio, new canopy materials, and a seven-point bridle that collectively deliver more speed, better drift, and improved jump performance without sacrificing the Bandit's signature accessibility. The dampened power delivery is the standout change — it tames the power spike that plagued previous versions, making it genuinely competitive in the waves while still being versatile across foiling, twin-tip, and freeride. At €2,100 for a 9m, it's a premium ask, but the performance uplift over previous generations is real and substantial.
pros: Higher aspect ratio and increased flight speed produce noticeably better jump height and hang time compared to previous Bandits
Seven-point bridle without pulley delivers excellent bar feel — direct, responsive, and comfortable simultaneously
Dampened power delivery via new canopy fabric tames the power spike, making wave riding and strapless surfing genuinely good
Excellent upwind performance with stable positioning at the edge of the wind window requiring no correction
Strong drift performance that holds its own against dedicated wave kites
Accessible to a wide range of riders, including beginners, thanks to consistent and forgiving flight behavior
cons: Steering lines go to a small V and are not adjustable, limiting fine-tuning options
Canopy stiffness is lower than stiffer-framed kites (e.g. Alula), so flight stability relies on material choice rather than structural rigidity
At €2,100 for a 9m, pricing is at the premium end of the market
structured_review.best_for: Riders who want one kite that genuinely handles freeride, waves, foiling, and jumping without meaningful compromise.
structured_review.not_for: Dedicated wave riders or big-air specialists who want a purpose-built tool rather than a refined all-rounder.
structured_review.rec_blurb: The Bandit finally nails waves without losing its all-around crown.
